possible_risks.description: Lack of model transparency is due to insufficient documentation of the model design, development, and evaluation process and the absence of insights into the inner workings of the model.
possible_risks.justification: The card reports only benchmark scores and the fact of SFT via the LION pipeline, with no documentation of training data, curation, or evaluation details for this checkpoint.

possible_risks.description: Proper documentation contains information about how a model's data was collected, curated, and used to train a model, including any synthetic data generation processes. Without proper documentation it might be harder to satisfactorily explain the behavior of the model.
possible_risks.justification: The card does not state how the fine-tuning data was collected, curated, or used, so the behavior of the model cannot be satisfactorily explained.

possible_risks.description: Unrepresentative data occurs when the training or fine-tuning data is not sufficiently representative of the underlying population or does not measure the phenomenon of interest. Synthetic data might not fully capture the complexity and nuances of real-world data. Causes include possible limitations in the seed data quality, biases in generation methods, or inadequate domain knowledge. Thus, AI models might struggle to generalize effectively to real-world scenarios.
possible_risks.justification: The card reports only generic benchmark scores and no information about the fine-tuning data distribution, so it is plausible that the SFT data is not representative of all real-world uses.

possible_risks.description: AI model risks are socio-technical, so their testing needs input from a broad set of disciplines and diverse testing practices.
possible_risks.justification: The card reports only standard text benchmarks (Arena-Hard, AlpacaEval-2, MT-Bench, OpenLLM) and no socio-technical or diverse testing practices.
